Banyana Banyana - journey to the FIFA World Cup 2023

By: Cheryl Uys-Allie | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
...we follow Banyana Banyana to the 2023 FIFA World Cup in New Zealand & Australia

Unique Selling Point:
Behind the scenes footage of South African players signed professionally at international clubs.

Summary:
After Banyana Banyana's incredible win at WAFCON in 2022, the team secures its place in the 2023 FIFA World Cup in New Zealand. We share the personal stories of two player profiles, from seasoned international players, to another at the start of a promising football career.

Travel to De Aar (profile for Nthabiseng Majiya) - TBC
Archive from FIFA / CAF (WAFCON)

Linda Motlhalo

Script:


#6371 | Banyana Banyana – Edit script | 10 July 2023
Opening sequence: 40 secs – opening
VO: Banyana Banyana - mould-breakers - role models. 2022 African Football champions.
UPSOUND Desiree (00:12:34:00 - 00:13:10:14) Winning the Crown also gives us a lot more confidence, you know, beating Nigeria … really shifted the mental mentality of the players.
VO: Returning to a heroes’ welcome… and the realisation that success breeds expectation…
UPSOUND – Linda (00:15:16:23 - 00:15:48:20 (tension!) … before this World Cup Afcon the previous one, we always came second best all the time. We were so close yet to yet so far.
VO: With access to their final days in training camp… we meet the team and their coach as they prepare for an even bigger challenge: The FIFA Women’s World Cup later this month.
Desiree: 00:10:19:11 - 00:11:01:18 it's important that we play under pressure. It's important that we get tested, important that we get a challenge because, at the end of the day, we're going to play an opponent that is going to put us under pressure.
VO: A challenge almost scuppered at the eleventh hour…
UPS DRAMA ON THE DAY?
VO: …as a lingering dispute with the country’s soccer bosses erupts just days before they fly out.
UPSOUND from Danny J: contract should be done sooner
FADE to Black

THE STORY
Opening viz – sunrise Claire Link: cold morning, waiting for team … players arrive at camp…
Claire Link: It's early on a cold winter’s morning…we are at training camp where the final Banyana Banyana squad will be selected to represent South Africa in the FIFA 2023 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand.
Viz: Players arrive at UJ training grounds – music … off the bus and warming up.
VO: Players arrive at the Johannesburg camp from all over the world.
These are anxious moments for those on the fringe of selection; they have just THREE weeks to prove to coach Desiree Ellis and her management team that they’ve got what it takes.
Desiree: We always remind the players that your performance will select you.
VO: Few understand that better than this former player and three time “Africa Coach of the Year”.
Desiree: The beauty of this team is we can play different formations, so we look for players that can fit into all of that. A lot of our players are pretty quick up front. We also need players that are versatile, players that can play in more than one position.
VIZ & UPS: Every time when it’s a build-up they will press you
VO: It’s Desiree’s second Women’s World Cup as coach. Banyana didn’t win a single game last time round, but her team’s continental success last year has raised expectations - for the players… and the country.
PAUSE
VO: And the coach is pinning her hopes on rising stars like 25-year-old Linda Mothlalo. She’s jetted into the camp from Scotland where she now plays professionally.
VIZ: lead with NATSOUND OF LINDA in action.. What did you shoot with her visually?
Linda: 00:00:23:07 - 00:00:33:18 I think because my father was a coach, he used to take me to the games. So I think that's when I realized that this is something that I like and I love.
VO: Originally from Jo’burg’s West Rand, she’s nicknamed “the Randfontein Ronaldinho” - after one of Brazil’s greatest-ever players.
Linda: Back in the day there was no women's football. …I remember I was accused of being a boy because that's how good I was.
Claire 00:02:51:02 - 00:03:13:20 At what point did you realize that it could actually not just be the game that you love playing, but it can actually be a career choice?
Linda 00:03:14:02 - 00:03:23:19 I think at the point where I got selected to go play at the Olympics, that was the turning point for me that I need to take this like very seriously.
VO: It’s an honour that comes at a price: Linda, like so many other players at the camp, spends little time at home these days. She’s played for clubs in 4 foreign countries.
Desiree: 00:12:34:00 - 00:13:10:14 …Our players have matured over the last four years. You know, they've gotten better, the league has gotten better, not where we want to be, players playing abroad, doing really well abroad. So that experience will also help us… we know our players have matured.
VIZ: lead with NATSOUND OF ROBYN in action.
VO: At just 29, Robyn Moodaly is already a 10 year veteran of the national team having played at the 2012 Olympics as a teenager.
Claire: How did it all start?
Robyn: …at the age of seven with my boy cousins. So we played in the streets, played in the parks, and from there I had a love for it and just continued.
NEW VO: But, being a prodigy only takes you so far in this environment. Like everyone else, Robyn’s going to have to fight for her place in the World Cup squad.
Robyn: 00:02:01:03 - 00:02:12:19 Yeah, definitely scary. It is nerve-wracking, but this is what we want, you know, This is what I love. I love that thrill, of stepping onto the field, representing my country. And I just can't wait.
NEW VO: The World Cup will be played over a month, with the final in Sydney on the 20th of August. Banyana Banyana are in Group G, along with Sweden, Italy and Argentina. They’ll need to finish in the top two in their group to progress to the tournament’s knock-out stage. It’s a tough group and a daunting task… but not for everyone.
Linda se(00:06:31:04 - 00:06:37:16) I've been preparing, so why should we be scared? We've been preparing. We've been working hard.
NEW VO: We’re reaching the end of our first day in camp. As the tension and excitement continue to build ahead of the team announcement, there are no signs of the controversy to come.
MUST DIP TO BLACK HERE – run nats audio from the training footage under the black
LEAD WITH UPSOUND RIDHAA – I want you to come up
VO: The World Cup is just weeks away. A busy time for conditioning coach, Ridhaa Allie.
Claire: How are the players looking?
Ridhaa: You know, when the girls are on the field, they look good, they feel good and we can only get better. That's the most important thing.
VIZ & SOUND FROM TRAINING
Ridhaa: …You can be running ten, 15km, but am I making the right pass? Am I making the right decision? So everything comes together and that's the perfect thing about having a team. It's not one person. It's everyone working together to see what's best for the team.
Claire: Is there a difference between the girls that have had the international experience?
Ridhaa: I think there'll always be a difference, but it's nothing that we can't work on. Because they help the girls that haven't played international games.
Robyn: That intensity from the international level is what helps us step up to another level. And I think it just makes us better as a team.
UPSOUND – Ridhaa / Desiree on the field.
Claire Link: Competition escalates for the coveted positions on the world cup team. Behind me is the best of the best and they’re giving it their all but the reality is not all of these players will make it onto the world cup squad
Desiree: (00:01:37:12 - 00:02:13:05) …unfortunately, if you could take all of them, you would. But you are in a position where you can only take 23 players and if they do not get selected, that doesn't mean that they're never going to get a call-up.
Ridhaa: 00:01:08:14 - 00:01:40:04 Time is against us, but we're doing the best we can because it's also important that our girls' mentality or they are very professional in what they do.
VO: Anticipation builds ahead of what will be a career- and life-defining moment for the players. (PAUSE) .. And in the corridors of power, the sport’s top brass prepare for the World Cup team announcement unaware of the controversy that’ll soon engulf them.
Dip to black here, then pump up the UPS and music to build drama and excitement
PLAYER ANNOUNCEMENT – SASOL footage of Gala event (up sound).
ADDITIONAL VIZ…Linda (Club: Glasgow City FC), Robyn Moodaly (Club: JVW FC, SA) .. Nomvula Kgoale – Midfielder (Club: TS Galaxy FC)
VO: After weeks of uncertainty for some and anxiety for all, the team announcement brings a renewed focus.
Refiloe Jane (Banyana Banyana Captain): Since selection there is less anxiety, it’s been a tense 2 weeks building up to the announcement.
VO: But, captain, Refiloe Jane, and her team will soon be thrust into a stand-off with the game’s administrators that threatens to undermine their preparation and splits public opinion on Banyana Banyana’s motives and their methods.
NEWS footage and upsounds from the game v Botswana
VO: Just days before their departure, a contract dispute explodes into public: in an unprecedented and highly controversial move, the team refuse to play a friendly match against Botswana. Billed as a celebratory send-off, it’s hosted at what the players argue is a substandard venue on Johannesburg’s East Rand.
Yet more drama with UPS from the presser
VO: It’s an ugly scene: frustrated players and management, an embarrassed SA Football Association, and football fans split between support for the team’s cause and those accusing them of behaving like mercenaries…
Viz: Tsakane stadium. Press conf. Fans.
VO: The players insist it’s a matter of principle: Contracts remain unsigned, and confusion surrounds how the more than half a million Rand prize money set aside by FIFA for the group stages of the competition will be split.
Visuals and ups from the Motsepe
VO: As the hours pass, the country’s football fans are largely in the dark about the behind-the-scenes negotiations, unsure about the fate of Banyana Banyana’s World Cup challenge.
DANNY: Contractual issues must be dealt with earlier
Then, with less than a day to go before their planned departure…a deal is secured: SAFA announces the contracts have been finalised and billionaire businessman, Patrice Motsepe, donates an additional R400 thousand per player towards performance bonuses.
BREATHER
Viz: Back to training in camp.
Robyn: There's a lot of challenges, you know, off the field that people don't know about - your sacrifice, your nutrition, your sleep. Being away from your family and friends, that all plays a massive, massive role. And then obviously, your injuries and how you come back from that is vital.
BREATHE.. SEGUE BACK TO CAMP…FINAL ACT
VIZ SEGUE INTO INTRO SEQUENCE OF KOTZIN
Ashley: I think the last 3 to 5 years there's been exponential growth in women's football. I think you only have to look at firstly fan attendance..
VO: Ashley Kotzin is a leading local sports agent.
Ashley: this World Cup is the window. Global football eyes are going to be on them and the ones that do well are going to be picked up and potentially transferred for really big value and for big money, hopefully into big leagues around the world. And that kind of financial value that the players would be traded for, sold for can really add value into their teams.
Claire Link: It's crunch time for African Champions Banyana Banyana. They’ve fine-tuned their game and they’ve locked down their strategy, all in preparation to conquer the world stage
Refiloe (Banyana Banyana Captain) comment: really excited for the opportunity to play at the WC
Viz – bus at airport …
Linda – excited for the world cup and we’ll do our best.
Robyn – super excited to bring the trophy back.
VO: Elite athletes - arriving at a make-or-break moment. The contract issues laid to rest, they depart as continental champs, hoping to return as so much more.
The End

PROMO 1
VO: Banyana Banyana are the champions of Africa… now, they’re playing to become the champions of the world.
UPSOUND Desiree (00:12:34:00 - 00:13:10:14) Winning the Crown also gives us a lot more confidence, you know, beating Nigeria … really shifted the mental mentality of the players.
VO: An unstoppable force taking up their rightful place among the best of the best.

PROMOS 2
CLAIRE LINK: It’s crunch time for African champions Banyana Banyana.. they’ve fine- tuned their game and locked down a strategy.
LINDA: we’ve been preparing - it ís nerve-wracking; but this is what we want, this is what I love – I love that thrill, stepping onto the field, representing my country

PROMO 3
VO: Train harder, play with power and perseverance... show no mercy.
UPSOUND: LINDA: WHY SHOULD WE BE SCARED ……WE’VE TRAINED HARD
VO: They've been called South Africa's beacon of hope... the pride of the nation .. but what will it take for Banyana Banyana to win the upcoming World Cup?

PROMO 4
VO: They've snatched the coveted crown qualifying as the ‘Queens of Africa’ for the FIFA Women’s World Cup in New Zealand and Australia
UP SOUND: REFILOE: AT THE BUS: We’re really excited ………….from insert
VO: And now the moment is fast approaching for Banyana Banyana to put their mettle to the test against the very best teams in the world.

metadata.Summary: After Banyana Banyana's incredible win at WAFCON in 2022, the team secures its place in the 2023 FIFA World Cup in New Zealand. We share the personal stories of two player profiles, from seasoned international players, to another at the start of a promising football career.
